bibliographic.abstract: The high-pressure crystal structure evolution of CH3NH3PbBr3 (MAPbBr3) perovskite has been investigated by single-crystal X-ray diffraction and synchrotron-based powder X-ray diffraction. Single-crystal X-ray diffraction reveals that the crystal structure of MAPbBr3 undergoes two phase transitions following the space-group sequence: 𝑃 respectively. This result is contradicting the previously reported phase transition 3<sup>�</sup> 𝑃𝑃 → 𝐼𝐼𝑃𝑃3<sup>�</sup> → _Pmn_ 21. The transitions take place at around 0.8 and 1.8 GPa, sequence: 𝑃 phases are determined from single-crystal X-ray diffraction analysis which is later 3<sup>�</sup> 𝑃𝑃→𝐼𝐼𝑃𝑃3<sup>�</sup> → _Pnma_ . In this work the crystal structures of each of the three supported by Rietveld refinement of powder X-ray diffraction patterns. The pressure dependence of the crystal lattice parameters and unit-cell volumes are determined from the two aforementioned techniques, as well as the bulk moduli for each phase. The bandgap behaviour of MAPbBr3 has been studied up to around 4 GPa, by the means of single-crystal optical-absorption experiments. The evolution of the bandgap has been well explained using the pressure dependence of the Pb-Br bond distance and Pb-BrPb angles as determined from single-crystal X-ray diffraction experiments.

datasets.dataset_description: Measurements performed at room temperature using a Rigaku SuperNOVA diffractometer to determine crystal structure and lattice parameters up to 5 GPa.
In situ powder X-ray diffraction experiments performed at the BL04-MSPD beamline of ALBA-CELLS synchrotron.
Optical-absorption spectra acquired in a home-built optical setup to study bandgap behavior up to around 4 GPa.
